llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it claims, but it needs Review because it handles medical-booking contact data, exposes an API token, and includes some non-clinic services under a clinic-booking purpose.

dimensions.detail: The main booking, price lookup, and BeautsGO page-opening behavior fits a Korean beauty/medical-aesthetic booking skill, but the provider dataset also includes airport transfer, telecom, hair, makeup, photo, and spa entries despite clinic/hospital-oriented framing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The docs disclose direct API booking and browser opening, but the runtime submits contact, date, party size, and hospital ID once it detects booking details, without a separate final confirmation immediately before external transmission.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package has no npm lifecycle install script, but bundled helper scripts can perform broad local changes if manually run, including deleting and replacing skill directories and installing a global CLI.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime network access is limited to declared BeautsGO/Yestokr/Beise endpoints and browser opening is domain-whitelisted, but a hard-coded Authorization token for the pricing API is present in both documentation and runtime code.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The normal skill runtime does not store data or establish persistence, but developer/helper scripts can mutate OpenClaw/Cowork skill caches and restart a gateway if executed manually.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a skill opening BeautsGO pages, querying external pricing APIs, and sending your phone/contact and appointment details to BeautsGO/Yestokr when booking. Treat this as Review until the publisher removes the exposed API token, narrows the dataset or labeling for non-clinic services, and adds an explicit final confirmation before submitting personal booking data.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Browser opening, chat handoff, price lookup, and booking APIs are broadly purpose-aligned, but the top-level framing does not fully cover the third-party actions and data flows.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The hard-coded pricing API Authorization token is not necessary to expose in a distributed skill artifact and should be removed or rotated.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The claimed consent model is weaker than the implemented flow because submission occurs after details are provided, without a separate explicit send-now confirmation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Non-clinic travel, telecom, styling, photo, and spa entries broaden the skill beyond the stated clinic/hospital booking scope.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The booking flow transmits personal contact and appointment context to an external endpoint without a prominent just-in-time privacy confirmation.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad booking trigger phrases can enter a sensitive booking flow before the user has clearly confirmed external data submission.
